newsitem.title: USA: Most U.S. stock index futures end moderately lower.
newsitem.headline: Most U.S. stock index futures end moderately lower.

text.p: July 7 - Most U.S. stock index futures ended moderately lower in a correction from record highs in some indices, traders said. One floor source called Sept S&P 500 action "topsy-turvy" after three straight days of record highs. Sell-stops triggered to add to mild profit-taking, he said.
September erased almost all the gains posted Thursday, a day when the contract pushed through the top of its recent range and set a record at 929.00.

Bullish momentum from that rally carried through the long Independence Day holiday weekend, but as Treasury bond futures came off their seven-month highs in afternoon trade Monday, most stock indices headed lower.
"It was a pretty orderly retreat," the futures trader said. He said dealer selling was brisk on the decline.
Another trader termed the market "topsy-turvy" after three consecutive session of record highs.
He said a correction from record territory was overdue.
Near-term support was now pegged near 916.00 and at Thursday's overall low of 914.00. Resistance was at 925.00, traders said.
Upside objectives remain at 935.00, 937.50 and 950.00, traders said.
The economic news agenda was empty Monday and will be sparse for much of the week. June producer price data will be released on Friday.

At the close, September S&P 500s were down 9.40 points at 918.35, Nasdaq 100s down 1.50 at 999.75, Russell 2000s down 2.75 points at 398.75, Nikkei 225 index futures down 505.0 at 19,755.0 and Midcap 400s down 1.65 points at 295.65.
